topics.label: Introduction and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture within the cancer course and sets out its learning objectives.

topics.label: Mutation-driven cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations arising in susceptible cells can support clonal evolution toward cancer in a permissive microenvironment.

topics.label: Environmental contributions to cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the evidence and uncertainty surrounding environmental contributions to cancer rather than attributing it solely to chance or inherited predisposition.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections can drive cancer, with Burkitt lymphoma illustrating the interaction between pathogens and cellular changes.

topics.label: Mechanisms of carcinogen-induced DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how environmental carcinogens damage DNA and generate mutations, including the influence of metabolic activation on their effects.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish mutation-producing initiation from the promotional conditions that enable initiated cells to proliferate into tumours.

topics.label: Developmental and tissue-specific susceptibility to carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cellular context affects susceptibility to carcinogens and consolidate that principle within the preceding account of carcinogenic mechanisms.

topics.label: Assessing carcinogen exposure and carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine methods for establishing carcinogenic effects and the limitations of the evidence those methods provide.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This closing recaps the lecture's conclusions and frames their practical significance as decisions about risks and benefits.
